subproblem.title: The scalar components θ·ξ(α) of an integer multiplicity triple are H^n-integrable on compact pieces of the carrier
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and U, K ⊆ ℝ^P. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (R : IMRep U n), with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ and ξ = R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_n = MultiVector P n. Assume K is compact and K ⊆ U. Then for every n-covector α ∈ Λ^n = Covector (Euclid P) n, the real function x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) is integrable on M ∩ K with respect to H^n = μHE[n] (Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure). In Lean: IntegrableOn (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x α) (R.carrier ∩ K) μHE[n].
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, IntegrableOn (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x α) (R.carrier ∩ K) μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2–4 of the parent proof (finiteness of θ H^n on a compact piece, and the domination |θ ξ(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ θ). Here they are stated for an arbitrary compact K ⊆ U; the parent uses K = closure W.
This proof uses the sibling unit_orientation_bounds: every ξ_0 ∈ Λ_n with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_0 Q satisfies ξ_0 ≠ 0 and ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1.
Notation.
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient.
- Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n and Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ, both with operator norms.
- H^n := μHE[n] and μ := H^n⌞(M ∩ K) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ K).
- Fix α ∈ Λ^n and put f(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
By definition, IntegrableOn f (M ∩ K) H^n means that f is μ-integrable.
Fields of R used: measurable_mult, locallyIntegrable_mult, aestronglyMeasurable_orient, orients.
1. θ is μ-integrable.
- The map x ↦ (θ(x) : [0,∞]) is measurable. It is the composition of the measurable θ : ℝ^P → ℕ with the cast ℕ → [0,∞], and every map out of ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat).
- K is compact and K ⊆ U, so locallyIntegrable_mult gives ∫⁻ (θ(x) : [0,∞]) dμ(x) = ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n ≠ ∞.
- Therefore x ↦ (θ(x) : [0,∞]).toReal is μ-integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top), and (θ(x) : [0,∞]).toReal = (θ(x) : ℝ).
So the real function x ↦ θ(x) is μ-integrable, and so is its constant multiple x ↦ ‖α‖·θ(x) (Integrable.const_mul).
2. ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 μ-a.e. By orients, for H^n⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q of ℝ^P with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. By unit_orientation_bounds, ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for H^n⌞M-a.e. x. Since M ∩ K ⊆ M, μ ≤ H^n⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono), so ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for μ-a.e. x (ae_mono).
3. Domination. θ(x) is a natural number, so θ(x) ≥ 0 and |θ(x)| = θ(x). The operator-norm inequality gives |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). With step 2, for μ-a.e. x:
|f(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(α)| ≤ θ(x)·‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ ≤ θ(x)·1·‖α‖ = ‖α‖·θ(x).
4. Measurability.
- ξ is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_orient), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure with μ ≤ H^n⌞M).
- The evaluation L ↦ L(α), Λ_n → ℝ, is continuous linear (ContinuousLinearMap.apply). So x ↦ ξ(x)(α) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable).
- The real function x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable (as in step 1, via measurable_from_nat). So the product f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
5. Conclusion. f is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 4), |f| ≤ ‖α‖·θ μ-a.e. (step 3), and ‖α‖·θ is μ-integrable (step 1). By domination (Integrable.mono'), f is μ-integrable, i.e. IntegrableOn f (M ∩ K) H^n.
proof_key_steps: locallyIntegrable_mult on the compact K ⊆ U gives ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞, so θ (as a real function) is integrable for μ = H^n⌞(M ∩ K) (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top).
orients and unit_orientation_bounds give ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 H^n⌞M-a.e., hence μ-a.e. (restrict_mono, ae_mono).
θ·ξ(α) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_orient, continuous evaluation at α, measurable θ).
Integrable.mono' with the integrable majorant ‖α‖ θ yields IntegrableOn (θ·ξ(α)) (M ∩ K) H^n.

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the restricted Hausdorff measure match the prose. Compact local integrability yields integrable real multiplicity; measurable evaluation and the transferred orientation bound give an integrable majorant for θ·ξ(α). Domination proves the exact conclusion. Its declared dependency on unit_orientation_bounds is sufficient and correctly directed.
